currentState.focus: Survey: Grosshans criterion for non-reductive invariant theory

knowledge.progressSummary: SURVEYED: Created Hilbert14NonReductive.lean (235 lines, 0 sorries, 1 axiom). Formalized Reynolds operator, Grosshans subgroup criterion, known cases. Key finding: no purely group-theoretic characterization exists - the answer is representation-dependent (Grosshans 1997).
builtItems: reynolds_idempotent: proved Reynolds operator is a retraction
finite_group_grosshans: finite groups are always Grosshans
insights: No purely group-theoretic criterion: same non-reductive group can have fg invariants for some reps and not others
Grosshans criterion (1997): H <= G (reductive) has fg invariants for all reps iff k[G/H] is fg
Reynolds operator is the dividing line: reductive groups have one, non-reductive dont
G_a is the critical case: fg for <= 3 vars (Weitzenbock 1932), not always fg for >= 4 (Daigle-Freudenburg 1999)
Full formalization blocked by Mathlib gaps: AlgebraicGroup, Representation, GIT quotient infrastructure missing
nextSteps: When Mathlib adds AlgebraicGroup: remove grosshans_characterization axiom and prove it
Could formalize Weitzenbock theorem for G_a on k[x,y] (tractable without algebraic groups)
Could formalize explicit Reynolds operator for finite groups using Finset.sum
